text:
maria: quick design review — prototype for the inline stop+regenerate control in Playground. thinking: put a tiny pill to the right of the streaming response that shows a small token countdown and two actions (stop · regenerate). link to fig: https://figma.redwood/xyz :eyes:

jon: nice. +1 for inline affordance. quick nit — 'token countdown' wording might freak people out (they'll think we're charging fewer tokens). maybe 'estimated tokens left' or a tooltip that explains it.

ashley: accessibility things: the pill needs an aria-label that explains state ("streaming, 24 tokens left, press to stop"). also make the regen a separate button so keyboard users can tab to it. we should avoid icons-only for those actions.

sam: for mobile, the pill could be too close to reply actions. propose we collapse to a single chevron that opens a mini-menu with stop/regenerate/details. desktop keeps inline.

maria: good call on copy — initial microcopy suggestion: "Streaming — ~24 estimated tokens remaining". tooltip: "Estimate based on prompt + generated tokens; final billing may vary."

jon: about the countdown: do we compute estimated remaining tokens by model max length - tokens_emitted? that leaks max context length. maybe show a relative progress instead (e.g., "25% of response cap") or a simple dot that grows.

ashley: progress alone isn't great for screen reader users. if we do percent, include text like "25% of response cap used". for regen button, use aria-pressed semantics? regen is not toggle so use role=button with aria-label="Regenerate response".

sam: I sketched a compact layout — attaching ascii: `[[1mStreaming [0m • 24 est] [Stop] [Regenerate]` — Stop should be secondary, Regenerate primary.

maria: design-bot, can you run quick contrast check on the pill background + text? also add hover states for both actions.

design-bot: Contrast pass complete: default pill has 3.4:1 with body text — below 4.5:1. Recommend darkening text or increasing pill opacity. See patch: token-pill/#a11y-fix.

jon: regarding prompt library integration — clicking the token count could open a tiny overlay showing which prompt in the library contributed tokens and allow swapping a shorter prompt. helpful for power users.

ashley: +1 but ensure that overlay is dismissible with Esc and traps focus while open. also keyboard shortcut suggestion: Ctrl+K to open prompt switcher from that overlay.

maria: next steps: ashley to draft final ARIA labels and keyboard flows, jon to prototype hover/tooltips and promptlib overlay, sam to produce mobile collapsed pattern, i'll update figma copy and run one more accessibility pass. aim for a small experiment release behind a feature flag.

sam: timeline OK — i'll have mobile sketches by EOD tomorrow.

jon: I'll wire up a quick storybook component for the pill and share.

ashley: drafting ARIA snippets now. example for stop button: ```html
<button aria-label="Stop streaming response" aria-live="polite">Stop</button>
```

maria: perfect — thanks all. tagging followups in the design task: https://redwood/tasks/PL-1234 :thumbsup:

jon: small question: do we want to persist the token countdown preference per user? maybe opt-out in settings because some folks don't want it.

maria: yes, make it a user toggle in Preferences > Playground > "Show estimated tokens" default ON for new users, off for existing.

design-bot: Thread archived after 2 days of inactivity (automated).
